sections.html:
Auburn is a city in Lee County, in the eastern part of Alabama, and it is the largest city in that part of the state. It lies in western Lee County, bordered by Opelika to the northeast and by Chambers County to the north, and it stretches south to the Macon County line.

The city sits at 696 feet and covers 62.07 square miles. It is the principal city of the Auburn metropolitan area, which had 193,773 residents in 2020 and belongs to the larger Columbus, Auburn and Opelika combined statistical area.

sections.h2: How did Auburn become a college town?
sections.html:
Settlers from Harris County, Georgia arrived in the winter of 1836 and planned a town that would be a religious and educational center. Auburn was incorporated on February 2, 1839.

In 1856 the legislature chartered a Methodist college, the East Alabama Male College, which opened in 1859 and is now Auburn University. The state took it over in 1872 and renamed it the Alabama Agricultural and Mechanical College under the federal Morrill Act. In 1892 it became the first four-year college in Alabama to admit women, and it took the name Auburn University in 1960.

Interstate 85 construction, which began in 1957, tied the town to the state's larger cities and let the university host more home football games locally. That history explains why so much of the housing stock is built around campus life.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Auburn?
sections.html:
Auburn has grown to nearly three times its 1980 size, and the 2020 census counted 76,143 people. The city's own housing market runs on students and families at the same time, and the figures show it.

A median age of 24.6 means a large share of homes here are rented to students. Many owners are investors or parents who bought a house for a child and now want out.

sections.h2: Who are the big employers in Auburn?
sections.html:
The economy is centered on Auburn University, which employed 13,545 people as of 2024, plus services that depend on it. The Auburn and Opelika area had a 3.1 unemployment rate in February 2025.

Outside the university, the city has built a base of mid-sized high-tech manufacturing and research firms across one industrial park and four technology parks. Manufacturing accounts for roughly 5,000 jobs. The Kia plant is about 35 miles east on I-85 and the Hyundai plant about 55 miles west.

The university's football calendar also moves the local economy. On home game weekends the city can see more than 100,000 visitors, with Jordan-Hare Stadium seating 87,451. A house close to campus can look very different on game day than it does in July.

Public schools in the city belong to Auburn City Schools, which has 14 campuses and more than 9,400 students. It includes ten elementary schools, two middle schools, a junior high and one high school, with a second high school planned to open in August 2028.

Elementary zones are set in pairs, with one school serving kindergarten through second grade and the other third through fifth. The district has been ranked among the strongest in the state, and school zoning is one of the first things a family asks about, so have the zone ready when you describe your house.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and what should a seller check?
sections.html:
Auburn has a humid subtropical climate. Average rainfall is 52.6 inches a year, and severe thunderstorms with damaging winds or large hail are common from late winter through early summer. Tornadoes are a risk, and Hurricanes Opal in 1995 and Ivan in 2004 sent torrential rain and high winds to the area.

Before you list or sell, walk the property and look at:

  • Roof age and hail damage on shingles, vents and gutters.
  • Water staining on ceilings or around windows after heavy rain.
  • Drainage near the foundation, which matters on a hilly lot.
  • Large trees near the house, garage or power line.

The terrain is varied: rolling plains in the southwest, sandy soil and pine forest on the coastal plain, and rugged forested hills in the north. Drainage and slope can differ a great deal from one side of town to the other.

sections.h2: How does the terrain around Auburn shape a lot?
sections.html:
Auburn sits on the Fall Line, where the Piedmont plateau meets the coastal plain, and its elevation runs from 386 feet at Chewacla Creek to 845 feet near the Chambers County line. That range means two houses in the same city can face very different slope, soil and water.

  • The southwest and west are rolling plains used for cattle grazing and ranching.
  • The south is coastal plain with sandy soil and pine forest.
  • The north has thick forest, high hills and deep hollows.
  • Three creek systems drain the city: Chewacla and Opintlocco, Saugahatchee, and Sandy Creek.

The city has 16 parks, including the 700-acre Chewacla State Park and the 200-acre Kiesel Park. The city council has eight members elected from wards, with a mayor elected at large and an appointed city manager, and growth and infrastructure are described as two of its main political issues.

sections.h2: Roads, utilities and who handles what
sections.html:
Auburn is reached by Interstate 85, US 29 and US 280, and it is heavily car-dependent with no city bus system. Auburn University Regional Airport serves general aviation, while Atlanta and Birmingham are each within about two hours.

  • Water and sewer: the Water Works Board of Auburn.
  • Electricity: Alabama Power.
  • Trash and recycling: Auburn Environmental Services.
  • Construction inspections: the Codes Enforcement Division of the Public Safety Department.

Codes Enforcement monitors construction in the city, so an unpermitted addition, garage conversion or extra bedroom is worth mentioning early with any buyer.

sections.h2: How does a sale close in Auburn?
sections.html:
On any Alabama sale the deed is recorded with the county probate judge, who calculates the state recording tax at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of that. The deed has to arrive with proof of the real sale price, and a mortgage that already paid its own tax is subtracted first.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the state revenue department. If you close near those dates, ask the closing office who pays the current bill and how it will be shown on the settlement statement.

Owners here usually choose among listing around the school calendar, selling to another investor, or taking an as-is cash offer when a tenant, a repair list or a move date makes a listing hard. We buy houses in Auburn in their current condition and you pay no commission, so you can compare an offer with a listing before you commit.

faqs.q: Is Auburn, Alabama, in Lee County?
faqs.a: Yes. Auburn sits in western Lee County and is the principal city of the Auburn metropolitan area.

faqs.q: Does football season affect selling a house in Auburn?
faqs.a: It can. Home games bring crowds that can top 100,000 visitors, so showings, parking and traffic near campus change on those weekends. Plan viewing times around the schedule.
Auburn City Schools serves the city, with 14 campuses and more than 9,400 students. A second high school is planned to open in August 2028.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Auburn rental house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell a house with or without tenants and without repairs. Keep the leases, deposit records and rent roll handy so the buyer and the closing office can review them.
